Minecraft Dungeons II Controller Mod (Mac, CrossOver)
====================================================

Plays the game with WASD, mouse and keys by turning them into a virtual
controller. The game itself isn't modified; the mod is one file
(xinput1_4.dll) next to the game's exe. The game must already run in
CrossOver (installed through Steam in a CrossOver bottle).

Install
-------
1. Quit Minecraft Dungeons II.
2. Double-click "install.command". It finds the game in your CrossOver bottles.
   If macOS says it can't be opened (it isn't from the App Store): right-click
   it, choose Open, then Open. On newer macOS: System Settings > Privacy &
   Security > "Open Anyway".
3. Start the game.

The installer also sets three CrossOver options for that bottle: use the
mod's xinput1_4.dll for this game, send the Option key as Alt (hold it for the
cursor), and keep the cursor inside the game window properly.

In game: F9 shows the key list, the backtick key (`) turns the mod off and on,
T starts typing (Esc ends it), hold Option for the cursor.

Change keys
-----------
default.txt holds the default keys. To use the recommended setup instead, put
author.txt in the game's Win64 folder (below). It only changes which keys you
press; the game's own settings stay as they are.

Or open "Key Layout Editor.html" (it opens in your browser). Pick Default,
Recommended setup, or make your own, then Save: it downloads default.txt,
author.txt, or wasdmod-MMDDYY.txt for your own. Put it in the game's Win64 folder:
~/Library/Application Support/CrossOver/Bottles/<bottle>/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/Minecraft Dungeons II/Dungeons/Binaries/Win64
(Finder: Go > Go to Folder, paste), and restart the game. The newest layout
file wins.

Uninstall
---------
Double-click "uninstall.command". Your saved layouts (author.txt,
wasdmod*.txt) are kept.
